svg.title: Lethal triad of trauma and damage control surgery
svg.desc: Hypothermia, metabolic acidosis and coagulopathy feed each other into shock and microvascular failure. Damage control breaks the spiral: abbreviated laparotomy under 60 minutes, pack bleeding and staple bowel, temporary closure, ICU rewarming and pH correction before re-exploration.
svg.text: The lethal triad feeds itself: break it early
Cold slows enzymes, acid weakens factors, bleeding deepens shock: one spiral

g.text: each corner feeds the other two: shock deepens

svg.text: DAMAGE CONTROL: STOP BLEEDING, CLOSE FAST, FIX PHYSIOLOGY IN ICU
1. Abbreviated laparotomy, under 60 minutes: pack the liver, staple hollow viscera
2. Temporary abdominal closure with negative pressure: no definitive repair now
3. ICU rewarm, correct pH and clotting, then planned re-exploration
Definitive surgery on a cold acidotic coagulopath dies with the patient.
Resuscitation-room cold is iatrogenic: warm fluids, warm room, cover the patient.
Transfuse balanced blood early: the triad starts before the theatre doors.
